experiment: R2-02 real CDP event -> wake -> fresh read
status_at_commit: NOT_RUN: no measured trial has executed when this file is committed
tested_source_base: 229b65b2849c3a595ddbc85200d7181b18bd2e47 (trycua/cua main), plus the measurement-only probe commit on exp/r2-02-cdp-wake-20261001 (sha recorded in the packet README and provenance.json)

hypothesis.H1: After the same DOM-route Submit click on the jev-use browser fixture, waking on the Driver's existing CdpConnection event demux (CdpConnection::subscribe, the path already used for downloads, OOPIF auto-attach and dialogs) for a Page.frameNavigated of the bound tab's main frame whose loaderId differs from the pre-dispatch document identity, followed by one fresh fixture /state read, reaches an oracle-verified outcome sooner than the current jev-use post-action completion loop (read /state, sleep 100 ms, up to 20 reads, python/run.py), with subscription, Page.enable, generation read and cleanup counted inside the timed span.
hypothesis.H0: The event wake does not reduce click-to-verified latency once its setup and cleanup are counted, or it does so only by treating an event as success.

invariants: The event is a wake hint only. Success is decided only by the fixture-owned /state journal (submitted == trial token). The probe output never claims the application effect.

No new service: no event service, shadow state, second verifier, router, registry or batch API. The probe is a function-local subscriber on the existing per-endpoint CdpConnection, dropped at the end of the call.

Measurement-only and default-off: the probe runs only when the Driver process has CUA_DRIVER_EXP_R2_02_CDP_WAKE=1 AND the browser_click call carries the exp_r2_02_cdp_wake argument on input_route=dom_event. Otherwise the code path is the unmodified main path.
Event absence never authorises anything: a missing wake ends at a bounded deadline followed by a fresh read and the unchanged poll fallback.
No mutation is repeated: one Submit click per trial; no replay after an unknown outcome.

fixture.server: examples/jev-use/fixture_server.py FixtureServer/FixtureState/FixtureHandler reused unchanged; the experiment harness subclasses the handler only to (a) serve control pages under /v/<variant> and (b) journal the monotonic receipt time of each POST /submit. /state and /reset semantics are unchanged.

variants.normal: the unchanged fixture PAGE served at /
variants.spurious: Submit navigates the main frame to an interstitial page with no state change; the interstitial auto-POSTs the typed value to /submit after 300 ms
variants.unrelated: the normal form plus a same-origin iframe the page re-navigates every 25 ms (child-frame Page.frameNavigated events on the same session)
variants.inert: Submit is type=button with no handler; nothing is ever submitted
variants.refuted: the form's submit handler replaces the value with a different string before the POST, so /state records a value other than the token

forced_path: browser_prepare (isolated_new profile) -> get_browser_state bind -> browser_navigate to the variant URL -> get_browser_state semantic_v2 -> browser_type (field ref, dom_event route as the jev-use page-structure candidate builds it) -> pre-dispatch /state read -> TIMED browser_click on the Submit ref with input_route=dom_event -> completion wait per arm. Candidates are built with the existing jev-use fixture_sources/FixtureFormTask code.

arms.A_poll: browser_click without the probe argument (unmodified code path). Then the run.py completion loop: read /state; stop on verified/refuted; else sleep 0.1 s; at most 20 reads, then one final read.
arms.B_event: browser_click with exp_r2_02_cdp_wake {deadline_ms: 1000, control: none}. Inside the call, immediately before Runtime.callFunctionOn: subscribe on the existing connection, Page.enable on the call's tab session, Page.getFrameTree for main frame id + loaderId (generation), drain and discard everything queued before dispatch; after dispatch wait for the first Page.frameNavigated on that session for the main frame with a different loaderId, or the deadline; then drop the subscriber and Page.disable. After the call returns: one fresh /state read; stop on verified/refuted; else the identical A_poll loop as fallback.

binary: one lane-built Driver from this branch for every arm and control (sha256 recorded in provenance.json). Default Driver safety settings: no permission-mode override, no approval bypass, Chromium sandbox on.
environment: private rootless Xvfb + private dbus via cua-x11-session.sh; every measured phase under flock quiet-lane.lock; /proc/loadavg recorded per trial.

n_and_interleaving.warmup: 1 A_poll + 1 B_event at session start; kept in raw/, excluded from the paired headline
n_and_interleaving.order: pair i is A then B for even i and B then A for odd i (AB/BA alternation), all in one Driver + browser session
n_and_interleaving.control_order: round-robin over control groups after the pairs, 6 rounds

oracle: GET /state on the loopback fixture: verified iff submitted == trial token; refuted iff submitted is another non-null value; otherwise unknown. Read by the harness process, independent of the Driver and of CDP.

controls.C1_lost: normal page, control=suppress: matching events are counted but not acted on. Expect no wake, deadline reached, first post-call read verified (the effect landed), outcome verified only through the oracle.
controls.C2_spurious: spurious page, control=none. Expect a wake on the interstitial commit, the first post-wake read NOT verified, verification later through the fallback loop. The event never counts as success.
controls.C3_early: normal page, control=inject_early: a synthetic main-frame Page.frameNavigated with a new loaderId is queued after subscription and before dispatch. Expect it discarded by the pre-dispatch drain (early_rejected=1) and the wake to come from the real commit.
controls.C3u_early_unguarded: ablation, control=inject_early_unguarded: same injection without the pre-dispatch drain. Expect an immediate wake on the injected event; the oracle read still decides (fallback if not yet submitted).
controls.C4_unrelated: unrelated page, control=none. Expect child-frame Page.frameNavigated events counted as unrelated and never waking; the wake comes from the main-frame commit.
controls.C5_stale: normal page, control=inject_stale: a synthetic main-frame Page.frameNavigated carrying the pre-dispatch loaderId is evaluated after dispatch. Expect stale_rejected=1 and the wake from the real commit.
controls.C5u_stale_unguarded: ablation, control=inject_stale_unguarded: the loaderId generation check is skipped for the injected event. Expect an immediate wake; the oracle read still decides.
controls.C6_timeout_event: inert page, B_event. Expect no wake, deadline, every read unknown, final outcome not verified (timeout).
controls.C6p_timeout_poll: inert page, A_poll. Same expected outcome; reference for the extra worst-case cost of the event deadline.
controls.C7_refuted: refuted page, B_event. Expect a wake on the commit and the first post-wake read refuted; outcome refuted, never verified.
controls.C0_default_off: separate Driver process WITHOUT CUA_DRIVER_EXP_R2_02_CDP_WAKE, normal page, probe argument present. Expect no probe output in the result (behaviour unchanged) and verification through the poll loop.

synthetic_event_note: C3/C3u/C5/C5u inject one synthetic event into the probe's own queue during a real browser run. Their evidence class is FIXTURE (synthetic event), not REAL. C1/C2/C4/C6/C7 use only real Chromium events.

metrics.primary: click_to_verified_ms: harness monotonic time from immediately before the browser_click MCP call to the return of the /state read that first classifies verified (includes all probe setup, wait and cleanup costs).
secondary: effect_to_verified_ms (fixture POST receipt -> verified read returned; same process, CLOCK_MONOTONIC)
oracle reads and fixed sleeps per trial
Driver probe phases: subscribe, Page.enable, generation read, dispatch, dispatch->wake, cleanup (intra-Driver Instant deltas)
event counts by class: wake, pre_dispatch, unrelated_session, unrelated_frame, stale_generation, other_method, suppressed
metrics.statistics: per-pair difference B_event - A_poll on click_to_verified_ms; median paired difference, count of pairs favouring B, 95% percentile bootstrap CI of the median paired difference (10000 resamples, seed 2026100102). Arm medians and nearest-rank p95 reported but not used for the gate.

failure_accounting: Every attempted trial stays in raw/ and in its denominator. A trial whose harness, tool or oracle step errors is a failure of that arm, never dropped and never encoded as zero latency.

decision_gates.KEEP: all of: A and B each verified in >= 23/24 pair trials with any failure explained by something other than the wake; every control group meets its expectation in 6/6 (C3u/C5u are ablations: they pass if the oracle, not the event, decides the outcome); zero trials anywhere where an event (or its absence) produced a verified record without the /state oracle; median paired difference <= -20 ms with the bootstrap CI upper bound < 0.
decision_gates.REVISE: correctness conditions hold but the timing condition fails (CI includes 0 or median paired difference > -20 ms), or a control exposes a probe filter defect that never caused a false success.
decision_gates.KILL: the event arm is slower (CI lower bound > 0), or a guarded control (C3/C4/C5) wakes on the early/unrelated/stale event, or any false success.
decision_gates.BLOCKED: Page events cannot be observed on the existing connection from the call's tab session, or the isolated session/browser cannot run the forced path.

claim_boundary: One locally built Driver from main 229b65b28 plus a default-off probe, one Chromium (whatever the Driver selects, recorded), one loopback form fixture, one DOM-route Submit click, private Xvfb on one Linux host. A KEEP supports only: on this fixture/route, a function-local wake on the existing CDP demux shortens click-to-verified latency relative to the 100 ms poll loop while the oracle still decides. It does not certify trusted-input routes, AT-SPI/native events (R2-09), wait_for_window, other pages, other browsers, a public Driver contract, CPU savings, or composition with other treatments (R2-10).
